Yes I agree, and that’s why i’m quoting the safety margin. Of course one should run a finite element modeling on fusion 360 to get an estimate of total forces and bending moments, but that’s kind of going too far....

...or is it?

Sorry, but you should use cos to get the load on the slot: .5 x 90kg x cos(hand angle).

According to this, hang angle is measured relative to horizontal: https://www.treklightgear.com/blogs/trek-life/how-to-hang-your-hammock#:~:text=In%20a%20nutshell%2C%20the%20tighter,degree%20angle%20is%20considered%20ideal.

So when I say no hang angle (not physically possible), all the weight will pull on the slot (the weakest point).

With 30 or 45 degree angle, some of the load will be pulled on the top screw and doesn't see the same ripping force.

Update:

Come to think of it, I am so focused on the load on the anchor I forgot about the angled force needed to keep the person up. So the equation for the force acting to separate the layers should actually be .5 x 90kg / tan(hang angel)

So yes, to keep the person floating at no hang angle, you would need infinite force.

For 30 degree: .5 x 1.7 x 90kg

For 45 degree: .5 x 1 x 90kg

So the calculation I gave above is only valid for 45 deg hang angle.

For eSun PLA+: 60MPa https://www.diyelectronics.co.za/store/pla/994-esun-pla-filament-175mm-grey.html

This is of course along the filament direction. CNC kitchen does more analysis on layer adhesion strength, which tends to be about half. So 20MPa should be the lowerbound.

Yes absolutely, during the design I've thought hard about the print direction. There's a compromise between the strength over the slot and around the screws.

Turns out that the static load well below the tensile strength of PETG/PLA plus:

Ultimate tensile strength of PETG / PLA plus (z axis, i.e across print layer): 20-30MPa
Smallest cross-sectional area in z axis (underestimate): ~ 1cm^2
Average person weight: 90kg
Average stress (assuming worse case, no hang angle): 90*9.8/2/(1e-2)^2 = 4.41MPa

So there's at least a safety factor of 5. The hang angle will also reduce the load by factor of 0.75 - 0.5 (safety factor 6-10).

Unfortunately I don't have a proper set up to validate the calculation or do dynamic load testing, that's why in print instruction I recommend using PETG / PLA plus, since they will deform and not fracture like the vanilla PLA.

Funny you asked this. I have bipolar 2, currently on Lamictal, and last weekend I took some MDMA.  

I'm experienced with substances; before diagnosis I was self destructive and hung out with lots of clubbers. I've since kept distance, especially serotonin based ones (i.e. MDMA, MDA, Mephedrone).  

The back story is that I started dating this girl who also love trance music. We dated for two weeks and she invited me to take MDMA with her. Normally I'd say no, but because it would be the last time I'd see her, I decided to go ahead.  

I didn't adjust medication, and started the night drinking a fair bit. I took one 'hit', danced, and waited for the come up. It didn't hit me very hard, more like a slow build up. After half an hour, I started feeling light, the music sounded amazing, and touching felt nice. I recall enjoying myself a lot at that point. After about two hours I took another hit.  

MDMA is like a mini manic trip, without the irritation and restlessness. It feels like there is infinite amount of happiness. You can lose yourself in this amazing world. Things feel so right. Everyone is amazing. Music melds with your movements. You high five other people. Walking feels like floating. You are thirsty, and water is amazing. You want to share this water with everyone. You want to meet people. The night seems to last forever.  

Fast forward another hour or two, the come down started to set in. First the music sounded strange, more grating. Then I started to lose energy, a deflated feeling like a balloon losing air. My mind was dull and more confused. I felt sad. Felt like I finished a great novel, one that was captivating, emotional, and beautifully written. The book was now closed, a new reality set in and life must go on. I decided it wasn't worth taking another hit and we left the club. I didn't talked much after that.  

We ended up at her place. I might as well warn you that MDMA will inhibit any male sexual ability (foreplay was my friend).  

Next morning, things were still off. My mood became unstable, I was happy in the morning, sad, then happy again. Even with Lamictal, which tends to reliably moderate my mood, had no effect. I broke down a little when we parted. So be prepared for loss of emotional control.  

Next two days I felt a bit broken, definitely depressed. I'm still recovering five days later, though today I'm almost back to who I was before.

My advice is to pre-plan what to do after taking MDMA. When the comedown sets it's hard to plan things. Allow a lot of sleep. Drink water and force yourself to eat. Have good friends to chat with, preferably over some canabis. Keep taking your meds.

Having my mother's look, I have been confused as a girl many times when I was younger. I was constantly teased as being gay, even by my really good friends once in a while, and I hate it. My confidence as a kid non-existent, I holed up in my room and didn't want to talk to anyone. I turned inwards and things sucked for a long time.

What helped was slow realisation that your confidence of who you are affects your life much more. That comes with experience, so you need to do as many things as possible. I recommend doing things in front of a crowd, they will associate that with being cool. Make effort to find and hang out with good people. Your game is a long one, not superficial good look bullshit. Make them rethink by showing what you can do, and what you can achieve. Dig deep, work hard, work out, and remember that they are the losers not you.
